summary:
OrdinaryAssignmentPolicy.select (policy ordinary-assignment-rules/1) is the only code that traces to the Proposed OR-first orchestration design (sections 4.5-4.7, 7.6, 8.2). It is a bounded policy candidate, not an optimizer, and it allocates, releases and dispatches nothing.

- Model: hard-constraint filter over every work x profile pair (capabilities with observed evidence, tools, skills, context, effects, outputs, reviews, recovery support, source-bound checks, deadline), then a joint fit check (named nonnegative int64 resources plus recovery headroom and all held reservations, slots = available - RecoveryCapacity, no writable-path conflict).
- Order: priority descending, original deadline ascending, then cost, duration and rework micro-units only when every profile has comparable economics (same currency and provenance class); otherwise a stable-identity fallback. Unknown economics is never zero. Work and profile ids break ties.
- Selection: at most 8 greedy passes and 8 selected candidates; a dependency must be satisfied or already selected. This is a greedy maximal pack under that order, with no optimality claim.
- Verifier: OrdinaryAssignmentVerifier.verify takes authoritative obligations separately, never calls the selector or shares its feasible-set construction, re-derives requirements, dependency order, per-candidate and aggregate demand, path conflicts, recovery slots and preference totals. Shared primitives are only validation, canonical encoding, units and path comparison.
- Bounds refuse rather than truncate: 32 works, 8 profiles, 1,000,000 evaluations, 512 KiB result.

The roadmap (learn-ordinary-assignment-kernel.md) calls the OR design 'accepted'; the design's own status is Proposed (see platform/or-orchestration-planner-stack). Reusable lesson: an independent checker with semantic mutation controls (pack entry optimization/certificate-checking). ADR-0098 §11 tranche 2 (FS-GG/.github#5245) lists this record; the generic technique is a pack entry, the FS-GG instance stays here (§10).
title: Ordinary assignment kernel: bounded greedy policy plus an independent verifier
